title: Which expressions count the stories read in eight weeks?
description: A child reads one story every day except two days of the week. The stories in eight weeks are counted from the reading days, and each of eight given expressions is tested against that count.
teaching_notes: One idea: the stories are the reading days in a week times the weeks, and taking the missed days away from all the days gives the same count. Watch for students who count all seven days of every week.

video_script.why: The child picks the expressions that describe a count of reading days over some weeks, by counting the reading days and testing each form.
video_script.substitution: Count the days that are used in one week, multiply by the weeks, and test each expression against that count.
video_script.anchor: A child who reads a two page story every day except Tuesday and Saturday, for eight weeks, and eight expressions to test
video_script.payoff_line: He reads forty stories, and the second and seventh forms describe it.

final_answer.spoken: he reads forty stories, and the second and seventh forms describe it

names.Ruhee: the child who reads a two page story every day except two days of the week

never_show: the value of any of the eight expressions before the answer
video_script.design: The eight expressions stay in two rows on the board. The matching forms are lit one at a time, and the others are crossed out with their reasons.

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about a child and his stories.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>Ruhee reads a two page story every day, except on Tuesdays and Saturdays.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>He reads for eight weeks, and eight expressions are given.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>How many stories does he read, and which expressions describe this?

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a week of 7 day cells with 2 crossed out; the 5 open cells repeated for 8 weeks in rows

marks.g1: seven day cells are drawn and two are crossed out
marks.g2: the five open cells are copied into rows, one row for each week
marks.g3: the crossed cells are shown as a group of their own

beats.colours: the missed days in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A week has seven days, and two of them are missed.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>We can count the reading days in a week, and repeat that for every week.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Or we can take the missed days away from all the days.

beats.on_screen: Given: one story a day, except 2 days of every week; 8 weeks; eight expressions

marks.gv1: the story, the missed days and the weeks are written
marks.gv2: the eight expressions are shown in two rows

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, Ruhee reads one story a day, except on two days of every week, for eight weeks.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Eight expressions are given.

beats.on_screen: To find: the stories read, and the expressions that describe it

marks.fd1: the words the stories read and the expressions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find the number of stories, and the expressions that describe it.

beats.on_screen: reading days in a week: 7 − 2 = 5; stories in 8 weeks: 5 × 8

marks.s12: 5 × 8 is written for the eight weeks

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, count the reading days in a week.
Seven minus two gives five days.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>In eight weeks, the stories are five times eight.

beats.on_screen: (b) (7 − 2) × 8: the bracket is the reading days, 8 is the weeks

marks.s22: the bracket is marked as reading days and 8 as weeks

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, find the form that counts the reading days first.
The second form is open bracket seven minus two close bracket times eight.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The bracket gives the reading days, and eight is the number of weeks.

beats.on_screen: (g) 7 × 8 − 2 × 8: all the days take away the missed days

marks.s32: 7 × 8 is marked as all days and 2 × 8 as missed days

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, count all the days, then take the missed days away.
The seventh form is seven times eight minus two times eight.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>Seven times eight is every day, and two times eight is every missed day.

beats.on_screen: (a) 5 × 2 × 8 counts 2 stories a day; (c) 8 × 7 counts every day; (d) 7 × 2 × 8 counts every day twice; (e) 7 × 5 − 2 leaves the weeks out; (f) (7 + 2) × 8 adds 2 days; (h) (7 − 5) × 8 counts only 2 days

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, see why the other forms do not fit.
<bookmark mark='s44'/>The first form, five times two times eight, counts two stories every reading day.
<bookmark mark='s45'/>The third form, eight times seven, counts all seven days.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>The fourth form, seven times two times eight, counts all seven days twice over.
<bookmark mark='s46'/>The fifth form, seven times five minus two, does not use the eight weeks correctly.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>The sixth form is open bracket seven plus two close bracket times eight.
<bookmark mark='s47'/>It adds two days instead of taking them away.
<bookmark mark='s48'/>The last form, open bracket seven minus five close bracket times eight, counts only two days a week.

beats.on_screen: check: (7 − 2) × 8 = 7 × 8 − 2 × 8, so the second and seventh forms agree

marks.s52: the opened form meets the seventh expression

narration: <bookmark mark='s51'/>Step five, check that the two matching forms agree.
Opening the bracket in the second form gives seven times eight minus two times eight.
<bookmark mark='s52'/>That is exactly the seventh form.

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>He reads forty stories, and the second and seventh forms describe it.
